title: When the Terminal Breaks Revisited
premise: Kestrel Reyes, a cargo navigator who once falsified a distress log to save his crew, is conscripted by the Concord fleet to investigate the Meridian, a deep-space vessel returned with its entire crew biologically aged backward. He discovers the reversal was caused by an experimental drive the Concord itself built, and that both fleets are being fed a fabricated story to justify war over the salvage. Torn between loyalty to his old captain—now a child aboard the Meridian—and the truth, Kestrel broadcasts the real logs during a reactor meltdown, ending the standoff at the cost of his own record and freedom; the novel closes with him stripped of rank but finally at home among the people he refused to betray.
about_author: Petra Nakamura is a former maritime radio operator who spent a decade relaying messages between ships that never met. She writes science fiction about people who keep secrets for a living.

chapters.title: Ballast
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. A routine haul through contested orbits establishes his weary competence and the sealed hold he refuses to open—the backup clones of his old crew. Emotional beat: loneliness disguised as professionalism.

chapters.title: The Ship That Came Home Young
chapters.summary: Kestrel witnesses the Meridian's arrival at Vesper Station: a derelict returning with forty crew members reverted to children. His hands shake as he recognizes one small face. Beat: dread and recognition.

chapters.title: Conscription of Convenience
chapters.summary: Concord intelligence officer Ilsa Vane drafts Kestrel because he flew with the Meridian's captain. POV shifts to Ilsa, who suspects her own command. Beat: reluctant alliance, mutual suspicion.

chapters.title: Children of the Deep
chapters.summary: Kestrel visits the quarantined Meridian survivors. The child version of Captain Okafor remembers things she shouldn't. Beat: tenderness curdling into unease.

chapters.title: The Lie That Holds
chapters.summary: Ilsa reveals the official story—a hostile weapon test—that keeps two fleets from open war. She asks Kestrel to help maintain it. Beat: the weight of complicity.

chapters.title: Hold Ghosts
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. He finally opens his ship's hold and confronts the sleeping backups, confessing aloud to them about the falsified log ten years ago. Beat: guilt made physical.

chapters.title: Salvage Rights
chapters.summary: A rival fleet delegation arrives demanding the Meridian. Kestrel watches Ilsa lie fluently and realizes she's good at this in ways that frighten him. Beat: admiration and alarm.

chapters.title: What the Drive Remembers
chapters.summary: Kestrel finds corrupted telemetry suggesting the Concord built the reversal drive deliberately. POV alternates between Kestrel and fragments of the Meridian's AI. Beat: the floor gives way.

chapters.title: Okafor, Age Seven
chapters.summary: Kestrel smuggles himself aboard the quarantine ward. Child-Okafor asks him if he kept the promise from the distress log. Beat: love against duty, sharpened.

chapters.title: Countdown Doctrine
chapters.summary: Both fleets maneuver over the Meridian while its experimental reactor begins an uncommanded restart. Ilsa learns her superiors knew all along. Beat: betrayal inside the institution.

chapters.title: The Backup Question
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Command orders him to destroy the hold backups as 'contaminated assets.' He stalls, buying hours he may not have. Beat: defiance born of loyalty.

chapters.title: Vane's Ledger
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. She audits the program's history and finds her own recruitment was engineered years ago. Beat: identity collapse.

chapters.title: Rendezvous at the Wreckline
chapters.summary: Kestrel and Ilsa meet off-station and trade what they know: the lie protects no one; it only delays a war someone wants. Beat: trust forged in shared disillusionment.

chapters.title: Small Hands on Old Controls
chapters.summary: Child-Okafor, dreaming in reverse-time, recites coordinates matching the reactor fault. Kestrel realizes the children are the only complete record. Beat: hope in an impossible place.

chapters.title: Interdiction
chapters.summary: Both fleets blockade the station. Kestrel is ordered to stand down; instead he plots a run through the wreckline to reach the Meridian. Beat: commitment past the point of return.

chapters.title: The Run Through Contested Orbits
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. A white-knuckle navigation sequence using skills established in chapter one. Ilsa covers his transgression from the inside. Beat: exhilaration under mortal stakes.

chapters.title: Reactor Heart
chapters.summary: Aboard the Meridian, Kestrel reaches the drive core and finds the countdown irreversible—but the children can be evacuated if someone stays to broadcast the true logs manually. Beat: sacrifice crystallizing.

chapters.title: Two Fleets, One Frequency
chapters.summary: Climax part one. Kestrel opens an all-band broadcast of the falsified-and-true logs as the reactor climbs. Both fleets freeze, listening. Beat: truth as a weapon that disarms.

chapters.title: The Promise Kept
chapters.summary: Climax part two. Kestrel stays at the console past safe evacuation; Isla's shuttle pulls him out at the last second, but the blast takes the Meridian and his record with it. Beat: cost paid in full.

chapters.title: Aftermath Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. Tribunals, resignations, the war quietly cancelled. Kestrel is stripped of certification. Beat: bitter justice, quiet relief.

chapters.title: Cargo of Small Passengers
chapters.summary: Kestrel ferries the reversed crew to a colony world, Okafor—still seven—asleep across the cabin from him. Beat: tenderness without debt.

chapters.title: Home Is a Heading
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Unlicensed but unburdened, he sets a course with no contract attached, the hold empty at last. Beat: belonging chosen, not assigned.
